calls.reason: The MIT/BU counterfactual study shows parts of GPT-4's reasoning can be tested without its training data. But it used the released checkpoint and tested single skills, not the paper's overall general-intelligence claim.

OpenAI's 16 March technical report, public before the post, disclosed a Transformer-style architecture, next-token pretraining, broad data sources and RLHF. That is little detail, but it is not 'absolutely nothing'.
OpenAI's launch post supports continuity in limitations, but its exam comparisons show large gains. The packet cannot settle whether the strengths changed in kind, so the result is mixed.

NewsGuard's 100-of-100 misinformation result supports the claim of unreliability. But OpenAI's published safety metrics and Bing's chat-turn caps undercut the 'no clear measure' clause, so the main point is mixed.
By March 2023, API data was excluded from training by default and gpt-4-0314 could be pinned. That left a workable route to test new private cases, so the claim that testing was killed is overstated.
